tactics.isoSummary: Show the isometric projection of the in-possession board
tactics.isoNote: Every dot above went through that pair of lines, from the same x/y metres the in-possession board uses — the projection is arithmetic over the board's own numbers, not a second set of coordinates kept in step by hand. Each marker carries the metres it was projected from beside the point it landed on, so the two can be compared without a screenshot. The lawn, the centre circle and the penalty arcs are the 2D frame's own Law 1 measurements, sampled in metres and projected point by point — a circle on the grass is an ellipse here, and computing that ellipse separately would be a second piece of maths to keep in step with the first.
tactics.isoNotNote: What this is not: a rendered scene. There is no camera, no depth buffer and no lighting, so nothing here can show you what a player would see — it is the plan view bent into a diamond, which is what makes it checkable.

home.metaDescription: FOOTBALL OS is a football operating system for fans, players and coaches. Today the AI player-coach vertical slice works end to end; the live football-world modules are still being built.
home.heroLede: One system for the whole football journey — follow the game, learn it, train against an explainable AI coach, and watch a player profile grow from real sessions.
home.moduleLiveBody: Live scores are not shown because no match feed is licensed yet. This module ships with M3 Football World.

home.featureTrainingBody: A library of drills with setup, instructions, coaching points, common mistakes and progressions.
home.featureCoachBody: Ask for a recommendation and get the chosen drill plus the reasons behind it — every answer is labelled demo vs live.
home.featureProgressBody: Completing sessions awards XP and nudges the attributes a drill targets, so your OVR is earned, not invented.
home.featureDataBody: Export your sessions and attributes, or delete everything you have stored, straight from settings.
home.policySyntheticBody: Player profiles, attributes and content in this build are synthetic demo data. They are not real athletes and are labelled as demo wherever they appear.
home.policyLicensedBody: No club, league, player imagery or broadcast assets are used or claimed. Anything that would need a licence simply is not shown yet.

One draw in twenty ignores the scores on purpose, so a stale memory can always be corrected.

manual.rulesTitle: What this product does not do
manual.rule1: It never shows real player data. Every world figure is synthetic, labelled as synthetic data where it appears, and recomputed from the stored rows.
manual.rule2: It never invents your profile. OVR, streak, best attributes — all come from your training ledger.
manual.rule3: It never shows machine guesses beyond their confidence. AI output is an estimate for training purposes, not certification.
manual.rule4: It never shows a score you did not earn. Your XP is the sum of your sessions; you own it.
manual.rule5: The demo world is labelled. Whenever a figure comes from seeded data, the page says so.
manual.rule6: AI availability is honest. When no provider is wired, the answers fold back to the stored arithmetic and say so.
manual.faq1q: Is any of this real football data?

manual.glossaryLede: Every word below appears on the doors you just walked. This page is the reader's own dictionary — for the world that the seed produced and for the one you will discover next.
manual.gSeedBody: The number the generator draws the world from. Same seed, same world. Change the seed, and every fixture, every player, every name re-rolls — the realism comes from the number, not the authors.
manual.gTierBody: The top division of this world's pyramid. Lyndera Superleague is tier-1; tier-2 is the step below, and the world's cup sits outside either.
manual.gOverallBody: The one number every player carries: a clipped estimate of ability. A 75 reading is three quartile. A 90 is rare. It never explains itself, but every match report reads against it.
manual.gXgBody: Expected goals. Each shot is credited with its probability; every xG you read anywhere on this site is computed from the shot, not from a scout's gut.
manual.gFormBody: Recent-performance pulse, back-calculated from the last stretch of minutes a player logged. A high form reading is not a talent attribute — it's temperature.
manual.gStreakBody: Consecutive games of the same result class. 'Three-match winning streak' means exactly that; the door that tracks it recomputes on every request, not on corpses.
manual.gUpsetBody: A match where the lower-rated side won. The door computes an 'upset register' for the tier — the days where the favourite's edge surrendered.
manual.gOriginBody: Where the figure came from: 'synthetic' for the generated world, 'user' for your own drawings, 'derived' for arithmetic on rows. Read it on every Provenance line.

tutorial.metaDescription: Ten doors, ten steps, the world explained at a glance: arrive, find your club, sit in one seat, learn how the world sees itself, read the manual — and come back tomorrow.
tutorial.title: Ten doors in, one good evening out
tutorial.lede: A football operating system is a slippery thing to describe. This page walks you through ten doors in the order a new reader should knock on them, and tells you, honestly, what to expect on each.
tutorial.honestyNote: Nothing on this page is gated. Every door below opens for a spectator; every claim below can be checked by pressing it.
tutorial.deepDiveTitle: What this product lives by, in four sentences
tutorial.deepDiveLede: If you take nothing else from this door, take these four sentences — they survive any rebuild of any feature.
tutorial.dd1Body: The world inside this product is a generated, seeded, deterministic football universe — no licensed assets, no real club infringements, nothing that pretends to be reporting about the Premier League. What you read here is the world the seed produces, nothing more.
tutorial.dd2Body: Every figure you can see is arithmetic on the stored rows. The scoring, the ratings, the upset register — all of it is recomputed on this request, not stored. If a number would be cheaper to make up than to compute, we compute it anyway.
tutorial.dd3Body: Every sentence on this product is authored in English and Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Arabic, French and Hebrew. Same words, same layout, same standards — never mixed.
tutorial.dd4Body: The world is stored locally. Your drawings live on your machine. Your stats live on your tables. Nothing about your game requires a cloud that you didn't choose to put it on.
tutorial.step1Title: Step one — sign in, or don't
tutorial.step1Body: You do not need an account to read. You need one to draw a board. Bring one if you have one; the door refuses nobody.
tutorial.step2Body: The training journal. A ledger of every set you logged, every club you walked in, every ball you touched. Your world is local and yours.
tutorial.step3Body: The world's mirror. Every door — the almanac, the story, the records, the matchday XI, the duel, the dynasties — is a recompute of the same rows.
tutorial.step4Body: The coach is the same engine with two settings. With a cloud key live, it calls a real model. Without one, it returns the player's own-row arithmetic — also honest, also useful.
tutorial.step5Body: The 2026/27 awards, the manager of the season, the top-committed side, the youngest bronze. All re-derived on every read from the stored rows.
tutorial.step6Body: The chemistry of eleven players. 10 shapes × 5 temperaments × 50 systems. Not suggestions — geometry you can measure.
tutorial.step7Body: 180-goal targets, mystery boxes, blind taste, freeze moments. The world's games you play against yourself.
tutorial.step8Body: The live replay stream. Every event of the seed's stored replay — not a broadcast — with pause as the honesty control.
tutorial.step9Body: Every feature, every gate, every door explained to you in one book. Read it after you knock; it makes the doors open cleanly for you.
tutorial.step10Body: You are now the reader the world was asking for. Come back tomorrow — the 2026/27 season keeps writing itself onto the rows, and this door is how you keep reading.

worldCreed.metaTitle: The Creed — the six articles of this world
worldCreed.metaDescription: The six articles the synthetic world lives by: the arithmetic is never invented, the real world is never mixed in, attribution comes first, no hidden god writes the scores, six tongues carry one voice, and your own machine keeps its rules.
worldCreed.title: Every world needs its own creed.
worldCreed.lede: This product is a fiction that was honest about being one — and a book of real football carried inside it, honest about being that too. These are the six articles it answers to, no fewer and no more.
worldCreed.a1Body: Every table in this world is computed from every completed match, one point and one margin at a time — no standing is written down, let alone imagined.
worldCreed.a2Title: The real and the synthetic live side by side, never mixed
worldCreed.a2Body: The 2026/27 world is not real football and never says it is. The Real Book carries the real World Cups and the real European Championships with open attribution — and no synthetic club namesakes into that archive.
worldCreed.a3Body: The openfootball snapshots this product reads live under CC-BY 4.0. Every fixture, every goal and every venue you see printed comes with the notice the source asked for, and that is non-negotiable.
worldCreed.a4Body: No script produces a result the world did not play. The upsets ledger, the dynasties ledger, the finals ledger and the almanac — all re-derive themselves from the seeded rows on every single visit.
worldCreed.a5Body: Every sentence in this product ships natively in six locales with no foreign letters leaking across them — and every key resolves in each of the six tongues at the count the catalogue itself prints
worldCreed.a6Title: Your machine keeps its own rules
worldCreed.a6Body: Wheel direction, reduced motion, dark mode — the interface asks you where it can, and where it cannot the /settings door lets you decide, once and for good.
worldCreed.footerClaim: The synthetic world does not pretend to be the real one; the real one does not pretend to be synthetic. Read them both.

coachHow.metaDescription: Every coach answer, node by node: classify, arithmetic, spend gate, phrasing, persistence — and the receipt to prove it.
coachHow.title: How the coach answers
coachHow.lede: Ask a coaching question and the answer is assembled on a fixed route — never improvised. You can see the route taken, the figures computed, whether the model was asked at all, and what got remembered.
coachHow.sixNodesTitle: Six steps, always in this order
coachHow.node1Body: A rule engine maps your question onto a stored intent (today, plan, weak foot, ball loss…). No model is consulted to decide what you meant.
coachHow.node2Body: Your profile, sessions and weak-foot rating become the drill or the plan. Figures are computed, not generated.
coachHow.node3Title: spend_gate — may the model be asked to phrase?
coachHow.node3Body: If the day's AI budget is spent, phrasing is skipped and you get the rule engine's own sentence. The figures stand; only the wording changes.
coachHow.node4Body: The model paraphrases the computed figures and nothing else. It never picks the drill, the plan length or the weak-foot tape.
coachHow.node5Body: Question, answer and route are stored as a coach message. Your next question can build on this one.
coachHow.node6Body: The pipeline stops. The envelope carries intent, confidence, and the graph_trace you can read chip by chip under the answer.
coachHow.neverTitle: Four things the coach will not do
coachHow.never1: It never invents a drill the corpus can't back — every drill reference comes from the committed library.
coachHow.never2: It never guesses beyond your stored profile and history — what you see is what it used.
coachHow.never3: It never spends the day's token budget twice, and never beyond the cap you set.
coachHow.never4: It never hides its route — the graph_trace is part of the answer.
coachHow.traceTitle: Read the route under every answer
coachHow.traceBody: Each ask prints its route as chips. If spend_gate says the budget closed, the wording came from the rule engine; if phrase_answer ran, the model only re-worded figures you can recompute.
